bibliography.title: FIRE: Frobenius-Isometry Reinitialization for Balancing the Stability–Plasticity Tradeoff

sections.title: Appendix C Implementation Details of FIRE

abstract_sentences.text: Deep neural networks trained on nonstationary data must balance stability (i.e., retaining prior knowledge) and plasticity (i.e., adapting to new tasks).

Standard reinitialization methods, which reinitialize weights toward their original values, are widely used but difficult to tune: conservative reinitializations fail to restore plasticity, while aggressive ones erase useful knowledge.
We propose FIRE, a principled reinitialization method that explicitly balances the stability–plasticity tradeoff.
FIRE quantifies stability through Squared Frobenius Error (SFE), measuring proximity to past weights, and plasticity through Deviation from Isometry (DfI), reflecting weight isotropy.

evidence.anchor: quantifies stability through … and plasticity through …

abstract_sentences.text: The reinitialization point is obtained by solving a constrained optimization problem, minimizing SFE subject to DfI being zero, which is efficiently approximated by Newton–Schulz iteration.

evidence.anchor: minimizing SFE subject to DfI being zero

abstract_sentences.text: FIRE is evaluated on continual visual learning (CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18), language modeling (OpenWebText with GPT-0.1B), and reinforcement learning (HumanoidBench with SAC and Atari games with DQN).

Across all domains, FIRE consistently outperforms both naive training without intervention and standard reinitialization methods, demonstrating effective balancing of the stability–plasticity tradeoff.
Explore codes and videos at project page: https://isaac7778.github.io/fire/.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Theorem 1
equation_theory_inventory.purpose: Under Lipschitz activations, m_ℓ>0, and spectral-norm factors, normalized feature covariance discrepancy is bounded by SFE.

evidence.anchor: SFE bounds output feature covariance between two deep neural networks

equation_theory_inventory.label: Theorem 2
equation_theory_inventory.purpose: With whitened inputs, bounded output Hessian/gradient, and a fixed ReLU pattern, Hessian spectral norm is bounded by products of ν_k=1+sqrt(DfI(W_k)) plus a remainder.

evidence.anchor: Hessian spectral norm bounded by layerwise DfIs

equation_theory_inventory.label: Theorem 3
equation_theory_inventory.purpose: For Φ=ZW and ε=sqrt(DfI(W))<1, the input-subspace spectrum and ε bound the effective-rank lower bound; whitening removes the η ratio.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Theorem 4
equation_theory_inventory.purpose: For isotropic Gaussian input and positive-homogeneous activation, DfI bounds every normalized neuron activity score.

evidence.anchor: Minimizing DfI increases neuron activity score

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 1
equation_theory_inventory.purpose: DfI controls each layer spectral norm through ||W_k||²_2≤ν_k and ||W_k||_2≤sqrt(ν_k).

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 2
equation_theory_inventory.purpose: ReLU covariance/spectral growth through layers is bounded by products of ν_j.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 3
equation_theory_inventory.purpose: Each block Jacobian and the concatenated Jacobian are bounded by products of ν_j excluding the perturbed layer.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 4
equation_theory_inventory.purpose: The Gauss–Newton part of the Hessian is controlled by β times the Jacobian bound.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 5
equation_theory_inventory.purpose: The second-derivative remainder is controlled by 2γ times products excluding the two differentiated layers.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma 6
equation_theory_inventory.purpose: ε=sqrt(DfI(W))<1 bounds every eigenvalue of WᵀW and the polar factor S.

evidence.anchor: A basic spectral lemma from DfI

equation_theory_inventory.label: Corollary 1
equation_theory_inventory.purpose: When output gradients are small, the Theorem 2 curvature bound is dominated by β times layerwise ν products.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Corollary 2
equation_theory_inventory.purpose: If DfI(W)≤((1−τ²)/(1+τ²))², every activity score is at least τ; τ=0.025 gives approximately DfI<0.9975.

claim_closure.claim: SFE measures stability and constrains feature-representation change.
claim_closure.method_response: SFE and the network-level sum are defined; Theorem 1 gives a covariance upper bound.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 5(b) measures normalized SFE but does not measure normalized feature covariance directly.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 restates principled stability–plasticity management without returning to covariance.

evidence.anchor: SFE provides an upper bound on the discrepancy

claim_closure.claim: DfI is a differentiable plasticity proxy connected to curvature, effective rank, and activity.
claim_closure.method_response: Theorems 2–4 and Corollaries 1–2 give the formal links under explicit assumptions.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 5(b) measures DfI and curvature only; effective rank and dormant ratio are not measured.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion recovers the overall tradeoff but not each proxy.

evidence.anchor: minimizing DfI results in a smoother loss landscape curvature
theoretical insights on DfI and loss curvature

claim_closure.claim: The closest orthogonal point jointly preserves SFE and drives DfI to zero.
claim_closure.method_response: Orthogonal Procrustes and polar decomposition provide the exact solution; Algorithm 1 approximates it.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 5(b) shows the lowest DfI and SFE for FIRE among compared resets.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §5 identifies constrained optimization as FIRE’s principle.

evidence.anchor: projection that simultaneously drives the spectrum

measurement_disagreements.name: humanoidbench_citation
measurement_disagreements.description: The p.9 HumanoidBench sentence cites Mnih et al. (2015), while the same paper’s abstract and Figure 4 context use HumanoidBench/Sferrazza et al. (2024).

statistics_and_visualization.aggregation: Curves/bar values are plotted over seeds; vision and LLM state 3 seeds, RL states 5 seeds, and Table 1 averages 10 trials. The exact center and dispersion definitions are not stated.
statistics_and_visualization.uncertainty: Figure 3–4 use shaded ribbons and Figure 5(b) uses error bars; captions do not name standard deviation, standard error, min–max, or confidence interval.

boundary_notes.layout: Double-column ICLR format; Figure 1 is in the p.1 right column, Figures 2–5 are wide/cross-column, and p.25/p.33 contain large unused whitespace.

final_judgment.single_storyline: Under past-data access, turn reinitialization into the constrained projection min SFE subject to DfI=0, solve it by polar decomposition, and approximate it with Newton–Schulz.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: SFE/DfI definitions, Eq. (4)–(5), Algorithm 1, three domains, Figures 2–4, and Figure 5 proxy/iteration evidence.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Proofs, module-specific scales, baseline instantiation, hardware/seeds/optimizers, compute table, iteration diagnostics, and hyperparameter search move to Appendix A–E.
final_judgment.best_pattern: The joint objective, mechanism-oriented Figure 5(b), and three data-arrival protocols put geometry, proxy, and behavior in one causal chain.
final_judgment.largest_gap: Theory is assumption-bound and only proxy-tested; rank/dormancy are not measured, the NS recurrence conflicts across p.6/p.24, the 1% claim lacks a denominator, and the main results lack numerical tables and defined uncertainty.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a stability–plasticity intervention, keep a joint objective, a mechanism-separating diagnostic, and a protocol that exposes post-intervention trajectories in the main evidence chain.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule fits reset/geometry methods with measurable proxies; it does not justify extrapolation to restricted-data regimes, non-matrix state, unsupported matrix shapes, larger LLMs, or fine-tuning.
